title: A perfect matching in the equality subgraph is optimal
statement: Let $G$ be a bipartite graph on a finite vertex set with bipartition into parts $X$ and $Y$ whose union is the whole vertex set, and let $w$ assign a real weight to each edge. Suppose $l$ is a feasible vertex labelling for these weights, and let $G_l$ be the corresponding equality subgraph. If $G_l$ contains a perfect matching $M^*$, then $M^*$, regarded as a matching of $G$, is an optimal matching of $G$ — that is, a perfect matching of maximum total weight.
hypotheses_covered: G is bipartite with parts X and Y
X and Y cover all vertices
l is a feasible vertex labelling for w
M* is a perfect matching of the equality subgraph G_l
